subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: What public capability taxonomy, grant storage, default-deny upgrade behavior, and enforcement boundary should OpenClaw adopt for skills/tools?
rationale: The item defines public plugin/skill metadata, persisted grants, security semantics, and compatibility behavior that cannot be safely inferred from existing name-based policies or hook-time governance.

options.title: Approve phased core capability model
options.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics, then design grants, enforcement, and audit layers behind an approved contract before any default-deny enforcement ships.

options.title: Limit to manifest descriptors
options.body: Add visible capability declarations for inspection only while keeping enforcement in existing tool-policy and hook surfaces for now.

options.title: Keep governance plugin-only
options.body: Close or narrow the core item if maintainers decide current hooks and external governance plugins are the intended policy boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve phased core capability model
recommendation.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics, then design grants, enforcement, and audit layers behind an approved contract before any default-deny enforcement ships.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent scoped capability profile work and issue discussion make this the strongest available owner for the security/product boundary decision.
